Fill in a PDF form in your browser

Open a fillable PDF below and type into its fields. Text boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons and drop-down lists all work, and Save a copy writes the values into the form's own fields. The form stays on your device the whole time.

If the PDF has no fillable fields, for example a scanned paper form, use the Text tool to type on top of the page instead.

Prefer it in Chrome? Install the Quire PDF extension

This tool opens your PDF on this device and never uploads it.

How it works

  1. Open the PDF with the Open button, or drop it on the tool.

  2. Click into a field and type. Press Tab to move to the next field.

  3. Use Sign to add a signature, or Text for anything that has no field.

  4. Click Save a copy. The saved PDF keeps the values in its form fields, so you can open and edit it again later.

Questions

Questions and limits

What this tool does and what it can't do.

Why can't I type into my form?

The form may not have real form fields. That is common with scanned forms and PDFs exported from word processors. Use the Text tool to place text on the page instead. Quire also does not support XFA forms, an older Adobe format that some government forms use.

Will calculated fields add up?

No. Some forms use embedded JavaScript to calculate totals or check entries. PDF scripts are switched off here, so those fields will not update on their own.

Is my PDF uploaded anywhere?

No. The page and its PDF engine (Mozilla's PDF.js) load from quireapps.com. After that, your browser opens, edits and saves the file inside this tab and never sends it to a server. The page has no analytics or tracking. To check, open your browser's developer tools and watch the Network tab.

Is it free? Do I need an account?

It is free, and you don't need an account. The tool adds no watermark and has no daily limit. Files can be up to 100 MB.

Does Quire keep a copy of my file?

No. The document exists only in the open tab. If you close or reload the tab, you lose any unsaved edits, so select Save a copy when you are done. The page stores two things in your browser: your light or dark theme choice and, if you tick "Save signature", the signatures you chose to reuse.

Which browsers does it work in?

Testing covers Chromium-based browsers such as Chrome and Edge. PDF.js, the engine underneath, also runs in current Firefox and Safari, but those have had less testing here. In Chrome and Edge, Save a copy lets you pick where the file goes. Other browsers download it.
